summary: Tracehook export dropping correlation_id for traces crossing retention boundary
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that when exporting trace CSVs from Console (Trace view -> Export) for time ranges that span a retention compaction boundary, some exported rows have an empty correlation_id column. Impact: Customers cannot correlate traces to API requests in downstream SIEMs and debugging workflows; several support cases opened by NimbusHealth (high-traffic dedicated tenant).

Observed behavior: The CSV export contains a mixture of complete traces and traces where correlation_id is blank even though the trace view in Console shows the correlation_id present in the UI. This appears intermittent and correlates with exports that include data from dates before a retention compaction (legacy partition) and after (current partition).

Environment: prod (us-east-1), dedicated pool for NimbusHealth.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Login as NimbusHealth user and open Console -> Traces.
2) Set time range to span retention boundary (e.g., 2026-02-26T22:00:00Z to 2026-02-27T02:00:00Z).
3) Apply tracehook filter: header.correlation_id != null. Confirm trace list shows correlation_id in UI for most traces.
4) Click Export -> CSV.
5) Download CSV and inspect correlation_id column: some rows are empty.

Expected behavior: Exported CSV retains correlation_id for all traces visible in Console.

Logs & artefacts:
- Example CSV subset attached by customer (sensitive removed): export_20260310_nimbus_sample.csv (customer-provided).
- Console trace UI link examples: https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/nimbus/traces?trace=abc123 (customer-supplied).
- Ingest logs around boundary (internal): s3://redwood-logs/trace-ingest/us-east/2026-02-26/compaction-manifest.log (referenced in investigation).
- Kibana query used: index=trace-* AND header.correlation_id:* AND @timestamp:["2026-02-26T22:00:00Z" TO "2026-02-27T02:00:00Z"].

Notes: Customer indicates urgency because their incident response playbooks depend on stable exports. They flagged this as blocking for a scheduled compliance drill.
steps_to_reproduce: Login to Console as NimbusHealth user
Set time range spanning a known retention compaction boundary (example dates above)
Filter traces by header.correlation_id != null and confirm UI shows correlation_id values
Export traces to CSV from the Trace view
Inspect correlation_id column in resulting CSV and compare against UI values
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 14:12 UTC - Support intake: Aisha validated customer's CSV and confirmed missing correlation_id values for ~18% of exported rows.
2026-03-10 16:00 UTC - Eng (Daniel) reproduced locally using internal tenant with synthetic traces and confirmed reproduction when export range spans compaction boundary.
Hypothesis 1: Export job merges rows from two storage backends (hot index + compacted cold storage) and CSV writer pipeline drops optional headers when merging different shard schemas.

Hypothesis 2: During compaction we apply a normalization pass that rewrites trace meta keys; earlier traces kept header.correlation_id under different attribute path (e.g., attributes.correlationId) and export transform failed to remap consistently.
Searched commit history for recent changes to export pipeline: found PR that touched csv-export merging logic merged 2026-02-25 (PR#4218) - candidate regression.

Logs show export job readers opening two manifests and using a union-of-fields merge; encounter: one reader emitted null for header.correlation_id when field absent in its schema; CSV writer incorrectly treated that as missing for subsequent rows during buffered write (race in field ordering).
Customer sample traces: the UI surfaced correlation_id because the UI uses a field-resolution fallback; export uses strict schema mapping - mismatch explains discrepancy.

resolution_notes: Mitigation/workaround provided (2026-03-11): Use Query API to run same trace query and request JSON export instead of CSV; JSON preserves explicit field mappings and retains correlation_id consistently. Provided example curl command and small script to convert JSON -> CSV for their SIEM ingestion.

Hotfix (2026-03-12): Deployed csv-export canonicalization patch to staging and then to a canary subset of prod exports. Patch ensures an explicit union-schema is computed before any buffered CSV write and enforces stable field-to-column mapping across merged readers.

Post-deploy verification: Ran a customer-similar export spanning the compaction boundary; correlation_id column preserved for all rows. Ran integration test suite covering retention rollovers and saw no regressions.

Follow-ups: Add synthetic test to CI for export merging across two schema-versions; update Confluence runbook to include guidance on using JSON export when immediate workaround is needed. Create monitoring alert to detect >5% blank correlation_id in exports for any org (ticket INT-2203 created for monitoring work).
Customer communication: Notified NimbusHealth on 2026-03-12; customer accepted workaround and hotfix plan, compliance drill rescheduled to use validated exports.
final_resolution_status: Fix deployed to production canary and scheduled for full rollout on 2026-03-13 after metric bake time. Workaround documented for customer. Monitoring alert and CI test created as follow-up tasks.
notes_for_engineering: Ensure csv-export pipeline normalizes field names from different storage layers before chunked writes.
Add unit tests that simulate readers with different schema-wiring and field ordering.
Consider making JSON export the default for cross-partition/time-range exports for a period until rollouts complete.
Coordinate with retention team to produce a mapping table for renamed fields during compaction windows.
